correctness.rationale: For nine explicitly bounded dyadic lengths, the proof combines complete factor-by-factor upper checks with rational dual-cover inequalities giving matching rounded-up lower bounds. The packaged standard-library verifier reads its own local certificate, rebuilds the Baum–Sweet prefixes by two independent definitions, enumerates all factors and factor-occurrence positions, verifies each dual load <=1 and ceil(total dual mass)=displayed optimum, and passed on the actual packaged paths. No finite-to-infinite inference is used.

value.rationale: The Baum–Sweet automatic word is a classical, structurally natural but non-uniformly recurrent test case; its exact dyadic string-attractor profile through 512 distinguishes it quantitatively from bounded-profile automatic words and offers a precise target for logarithmic-growth investigations. The nine optimality certificates provide nontrivial exact combinatorial information rather than a raw estimate or a known table, while leaving all asymptotic claims open.
